> **What you can defend when you leave.** Write the claim you can defend, bounded by what your evidence supports, with your AI use disclosed.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

Writing is where research leaves your head and can first be misread. This milestone turns your audited results into claims a stranger can weigh: each one bounded by what the design established, traced to the output that supports it, and accompanied by an honest account of what AI did along the way. The discipline is simple and strict. A claim with no row in the evidence table does not ship.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 9: Your bounded claims](milestone09-write-bound-disclose.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** A stand-alone research note or report draft, a claim-to-evidence table, and your AI disclosure statement.

Milestone 10 adapts these bounded claims to a real audience and rehearses their defense. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 9; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 28 — From Results to Claims](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/25-from-results-to-claims.html): your claims with verbs downgraded to what the design established, each carrying its boundary line.
- [Lesson 29 — Claim–Evidence Tables](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/26-claim-evidence-tables.html): your claim-evidence table, one row per claim with claim, evidence, trace, and boundary, every number traced to its output.
- [Lesson 30 — AI Disclosure and Research Integrity](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/31-ai-disclosure-and-research-integrity.html): your AI-use disclosure, written from the ledger and naming what you did not verify.
- [Lesson 31 — From Dossier to Research Note](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part6-after-conference/33-from-poster-to-research-note.html): your stand-alone note draft: the problem-gap-question spine, methods, results with uncertainty, discussion, ordered findings with the headline claim's boundary inside, references, your disclosure placed, and the pointer to the package Studio 11 will freeze.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
